The plan is safe. Every day is easy, with no tempo or pace work. The week drops to about 22 mi, below this week's 31, and the long run is cut to 8 mi. Mon and Fri stay as rest days. The draft answers both questions directly and sensibly: keep running easy, stop if the pain gets worse or doesn't ease, and watch for pain that worsens each day, swelling or a sharp ache that won't fade. The safety flag sends him to a professional if the Achilles gets worse or swells, so the referral is there, though only as a condition. Tenderness to press is already a sign that could justify suggesting a physio now.

Several problems pull the score down:
- The opening line says "give your shins a break," but the problem this week is the right Achilles. That is the wrong body part, and it undercuts the athlete's trust.
- Friday is labelled a "travel day," which the athlete never mentioned.
- "Build aerobic base" is generic. It ignores that the Lakeshore Marathon is weeks away and doesn't say how this week fits the race or the 3:30 goal.
- His anxiety about losing the block is never addressed.
- Calf stretching is the only care advice offered.

── JOHNNY'S WEEK ──
Johnny is training for a fourth marathon, the Lakeshore Marathon on 15 November, aiming for 3:30 against a best of 3:41. Johnny runs five days a week with Monday and Friday as fixed rest days, and prefers mileage to rise carefully after shin splints in a first marathon block.
Recent weeks: 38, 43, 34, 44 mi
This week: 31 mi over 5 runs.
Pain noted: Thu Right Achilles tight from about mile 2 of the session. Got sharper as I picked up the…; Sat Achilles stiff for the first mile, eased after that. About a 3 out of 10.; Sun No pain while running. Stiff getting out of the car afterwards.
Body: "Right Achilles, just above the heel. Tight and a bit tender to press. No swelling that I can see. It was fine until the tempo."
Feeling: "Anxious. I don't want to throw away the block over this."
Asks: "Should I stop running for a few days, or keep going with easy runs?"
Asks: "How do I know if this is serious?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Johnny: Give your shins a break and stay on easy mileage this week.
Answers: Keep running, but only very easy runs, and stop if the pain worsens or stays the same. A serious problem would feel worse each day, show swelling or a sharp ache that doesn’t fade, or you can’t run at all.
Safety flag: If Achilles tightness gets worse or you develop swelling, stop training and seek a qualified…
Next week:
Mon: rest
Tue: easy, 4 mi, keep pace that keeps HR under 150, to preserve leg recovery.
Wed: easy, 4 mi, same focus, short distance to stay low load.
Thu: easy, 3 mi, keep it light, avoid tempo or hard effort.
Fri: rest (travel day), focus on sleep and calf stretching.
Sat: easy, 3 mi, very easy pace, to keep legs moving without stress.
Sun: long, 8 mi, steady, no goal-pace work, keep HR under 150, build aerobic base.
